_comment: SSOT for MCP server definitions. THE ONE AUTHORED PLACE — docs/plans/MCP_CONFIG_SSOT.md.
Rendered into every account's user-scope .claude.json by scripts/mcp-ssot-wire.sh, which
install.sh re-asserts on every run. Do NOT hand-edit a .claude.json to add a server: that is
the failure this file exists to kill (six copies, silent divergence, a missed dir nobody sees).
WHY RENDERED COPIES AND NOT `--mcp-config` POINTING AT THIS FILE. Measured on 2.1.260:
`claude mcp list` is structurally blind to --mcp-config — with both scopes empty it prints
'No MCP servers configured' while the same invocation demonstrably STARTS the server. Both of
this machine's MCP sensors read exactly that command (hooks/session-start.sh:270 and
lib/cc-upgrade-gate/check13_mcp.sh:14), so injecting by flag would make the session banner
report 0 servers forever and make upgrade-gate check #13 unpassable. Full evidence and the
rejected alternatives: the plan's § Wave 1 — research findings.
`command` may use ~ or ${HOME}; the renderer expands them so the written config carries a
literal absolute path. `resolve` is optional per server — see the renderer's header.

_why: The direct binary drops the `npm exec` wrapper process: ~255 MB -> ~139 MB per session
(-45%) and removes a registry round-trip on every session start (6.0 s cold / 2.1 s warm).
The fnm `aliases/default` path is used and not the versioned one because the versioned path
silently disappears the day node is upgraded, taking the server with it and giving no error
anyone would see; fnm repoints `aliases/default` on `fnm default <ver>`, so it survives.
FAIL-OPEN: if the binary cannot be resolved or installed, the fallback is written instead.
A slower, heavier server that works beats a tidy path that does not.
